newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S.Africa's Tutu says needs more cancer treatment.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Tutu says needs more cancer treatment.

text.p: South Africa's Archbishop Desmond Tutu was quoted on Wednesday as saysing he had to undergo another operation or radiotherapy in his battle against cancer.
In an interview with Swedish newspaper Aftonbladet, Tutu said he needed further treatment after an operation last month to remove a cancerous prostate gland.
"I must undergo a new operation or radiotherapy," Tutu told Aftonbladet.
"I have not yet decided which. Offers have come in from the United States and several other countries to operate on me there."
The 65-year-old Nobel peace prize laureate, who retired last year as archbishop of Cape Town, said he had not realised he was sick before he was diagnosed as having cancer.
"I had no idea that I was sick before the doctors told me," Tutu said.
After his mid-January operation, Tutu's doctors said there was no evidence that the cancer had spread beyond the prostate, but they warned that he could still need further surgery.
Tutu is head of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission which has the task of uncovering human rights violations during the apartheid era.
